content.overview: Spectrum affects photosynthesis and plant form, but its outcome depends on PPFD, cultivar, developmental stage and canopy-management context. Advanced lighting decisions therefore compare full treatment combinations rather than naming one color ratio as universally best.

vocabulary.definition: Plant growth and developmental responses regulated by light signals beyond photosynthetic energy capture.
How emitted photons are distributed across wavelengths.
A response in which different genotypes react differently to the same environmental treatment.

sections.title: Spectrum and intensity interact
sections.body: Cannabis studies show that spectrum effects on biomass and morphology cannot be separated cleanly from PPFD and developmental context.

sections.title: Cultivars may respond differently
sections.body: Recent indoor work found spectrum and defoliation effects varied by cultivar, reinforcing the need to validate a lighting strategy on the actual genetics being produced.

sections.title: Yield, morphology and concentration are different outcomes
sections.body: A compact plant with high concentration is not necessarily the treatment with the greatest total harvested compound or biomass. Lighting trials should define the production goal before ranking treatments.

workedExamples: If blue-rich light reduces height but also reduces floral biomass, decide whether space efficiency or total yield is the more important target before calling the treatment superior.
If two cultivars respond differently to the same spectrum, maintain cultivar-specific evidence rather than averaging them into one recipe.
commonMistakes: Choosing lights by marketing spectrum names.
Comparing spectra at unequal PPFD without noting the confound.
Equating cannabinoid concentration with total cannabinoid yield.
content.practicalApplication: For any lighting comparison, record spectral distribution, PPFD, DLI, cultivar, stage, architecture, biomass and concentration-based outcomes separately.
content.summary: Spectrum is one part of a treatment system. Advanced photobiology interprets spectrum with intensity, genotype, architecture and production goals.
